title: You have a study list. What next?

parts.speech: You have a study list and some papers. How do you turn them into a review that people can actually check?
parts.headline:
From a study list
to a review you can check
points: How do you prepare the sources?
How do judgments connect to evidence?

parts.speech: These two skills help prepare full texts and organize review. Use them together, or start with the step you need.

title: Start with the materials you have

parts.speech: Bring your question, study list and existing PDFs. Include your protocol or codebook if you have one; a draft is fine.
parts.headline: Start with what you have

parts.speech: For example: find the missing full texts in this list and preserve the IDs. Tell me exactly what to do when you need my help.
parts.headline: Your first request
parts.prompt:
Use $literature-pdf-retrieval.
Find missing full texts for this list; preserve IDs and originals.
Give me a specific access step when my help is needed.
parts.tag: Example prompt · adapt it to your materials

title: Change routes when the evidence calls for it

parts.speech: The agent checks what you already have, fills metadata gaps, and tries available public, publisher or repository sources. Failed attempts stay in the log.
parts.headline: The agent tries available routes first
parts.footer: Keep each attempt so the next session can resume

parts.speech: If you have institutional access, it can inspect library resources and access routes. A direct paywall may not be the only route.
parts.headline: Adapt to your access conditions
parts.footer: A library link still needs an actual access check

title: Make the human access step specific

parts.speech: Sometimes the remaining step is sign-in, authentication, or saving a file you can open. The handoff names the article, page, action and return location.
Return the file, and validation resumes. Other accessible papers can continue meanwhile. A manually saved PDF gets the same checks.

title: Obtaining a file is only the first check

parts.speech: A readable PDF is not automatically the right report. Check the article or chapter, DOI, version and completeness, and record its pages and file hash.
If text extraction is unreliable, use another check. If identity remains uncertain, keep it pending. A filename is not identity evidence.
This stage delivers checked sources, attempt history and a remaining queue. If your full texts are already ready, start at the next stage.

title: People develop the rules and choose the rounds

parts.speech: Before coding, the team develops the rules. You might start with a small sample, perhaps ten reports, and discuss definitions that need work.
parts.headline: People develop the codebook
points: The project chooses the sample size

parts.speech: Once the rules are usable, AI can prepare the next batch for people to verify. You can return to calibration or choose independent review.
Assisted mode shows proposals and evidence. Independent mode gives reviewers the rules, sources and blank forms, without AI suggestions or other people’s feedback.
Here is the independent form in the fictional portable example. People can code first and return their answers. The team chooses the mode for each round.
parts.label: Independent blank form · fictional data
parts.source_note: Actual portable workbench · fictional report and PDF

title: Follow one judgment back to the source

parts.speech: Now look at the actual Pilot workbench. The item is in the middle, with the source on the right. Click a citation to reach its page.
parts.label: Start with the page citation

parts.speech: When a quotation matches, the reader highlights it. Then read the context and decide whether the passage supports the code.
parts.label: Find the passage; read the context

parts.speech: After checking, confirm the item or choose Revise and explain the change. These demonstration responses are stored separately from research judgments.
parts.label: Explain your revision

title: Give each reviewer the right task

parts.speech: Assign reports, fields, instructions and review modes by person. One reviewer might check methods, another concepts. The agent prepares the configuration.
Reviewers open their own package in a browser, then export a JSON file to return. They do not need an AI account or a shared login.
parts.label: Export and return the file

title: People resolve differences after returns arrive

parts.speech: The agent checks round bindings and coverage, then organizes differences. The research team returns to the evidence and decides what to accept.
parts.headline: From feedback to an authorized judgment
parts.footer: Completed feedback does not mean every disagreement is resolved

parts.speech: If a PDF or rule changes later, preserve the old version, identify affected work, and start the round that needs to be redone.
parts.headline: Changes can affect later work
parts.footer: Software flags registered dependencies; people inspect the rest

title: Two cases show what can transfer

parts.speech: TALL worked with primary studies; Agency works at review level. Their units and rules differ, while source links, feedback and adjudication can transfer.
parts.headline: Primary empirical studies

parts.speech: For your review, supply your own question, codebook and assignments. The cases are at different stages; they are not a controlled demonstration of time savings.
parts.headline: Review-level evidence

title: Choose an entry point and start your first round

parts.speech: Both GitHub pages include installation instructions and examples. Coordinators install the skill folder in a compatible agent; reviewers can first explore a fictional demo.
With full texts and draft rules, ask: prepare review packages for our chosen sample, explain the gaps, and identify the decisions our team must make.
parts.headline: Once the sources are ready
parts.prompt:
Use $review-evidence-workflow.
Here are the full texts, draft codebook and chosen sample.
Prepare review packages and identify gaps and human decisions.
parts.tag: Example prompt · choose your mode, fields and sample

parts.speech: The aim is to reduce searching, copying and repeated navigation, while people retain control of the rules, interpretation and conclusions.
